source_text: Principium Levitici: vocavit Dominus Moysen et locutus est ei de tabernaculo. Vocatio Dei ad secreta ducit. Non in Aegypto vocatur ad sacrificia, sed in deserto, in tabernaculo testimonii. Qui adhuc in Aegypto vitiorum est, hostias spiritales offerre non potest. Vocatus Moyses legem sacrificiorum accipit — non ut cruentis victimis Christum ecclesia immolet, sed ut intelligat holocaustum rationabile.
pass_a_gloss: Beginning of-Leviticus: called Lord Moses and spoke to-him from tabernacle. Calling of-God to secrets leads. Not in Egypt is-called to sacrifices, but in desert, in tabernacle of-testimony. Who still in Egypt of-vices is, victims spiritual to-offer not can. Called Moses law of-sacrifices receives — not that with-bloody victims Christ church may-immolate, but that it-may-understand burnt-offering rational.
pass_b_english: Leviticus opens: [[the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting >> Bible:Leviticus 1:1]]. God’s call leads into secrets. He is not summoned to sacrifice still in Egypt, but in the wilderness, at the tent of testimony. Whoever remains in Egypt’s vices cannot yet offer spiritual victims. Called Moses receives the law of offerings — not so the church may immolate Christ with bloody cattle, but so she may understand the [[rational burnt offering >> Bible:Romans 12:1]].
